506	### 5.15 AI Entry FAB (Host Page Surface)
507	
508	Floating sparkle button inside the host page's action bar. Single tap
509	opens the chat sheet at `half` snap.
510	
511	| Property | Value |
512	|---|---|
513	| Shape | Rounded square (`chat-radius-sm`, radius 10) |
514	| Size | 56 × 56 (matches base DS button height for visual rhythm in the action bar) |
515	| Background | `--primary` |
516	| Icon | Phosphor `star-four`, 24 × 24, white, weight 700 |
517	| Host bar position | Defined by host page's action-bar layout |
518	| Gap from neighbor | 10 |
519	
520	> **Note:** This is the *one* place chat radii do **not** apply, because
521	> the FAB sits *inside* the host page's action bar — a base-DS
522	> component. The FAB matches the radii and height of its neighbors
523	> (typically 10 px @ 56 h) for cohesion with the host page. Once the
524	> sheet opens, all chat radii apply inside the sheet.
525	
526	### 5.16 Desktop Floating Popover Container
527	
528	Alternative to the mobile Modal Bottom Sheet (§5.7). Used on desktop
529	viewports where the host page stays partially visible behind the chat
530	surface — context anchoring shifts from sheet-dominates-screen (mobile)
531	to popover-overlays-corner (desktop). Same 12-state machine, same chat
532	tokens; the container shell is what differs.
533	
534	| Property | Value |
535	|---|---|
536	| Container | Fixed-position floating panel anchored to viewport bottom-right |
537	| `cornerRadius` | 16 (`chat-radius-md`, **all four corners** — not sheet-style top-only) |
538	| Background | `--card` |
539	| Width | 400 px (`max-width: calc(100vw - 48px)`) |
540	| Height | 600 px (`max-height: calc(100vh - 48px)`) |
541	| Right offset | 24 px |
542	| Bottom offset | 24 px |
543	| Drop shadow | `0 12 40 / 22%` outer — replaces the mobile scrim |
544	| Scrim | **None** — host page remains interactive behind the popover |
545	| z-index | 1000 |
546	| Transition | `opacity 0.22s, transform 0.22s` (rise from bottom-right with `scale(0.97)`) |
547	| Snap points | **None** — width/height are fixed, no drag-to-resize gesture |
548	| Drag bar / grabber | **None** — close exclusively via the `×` button or ESC key |
549	| Safe-area-inset | **N/A** — desktop has no notch / home indicator |
550	
551	**FAB / panel toggle:** the desktop FAB lives at the same `bottom: 24px;
552	right: 24px` slot. When the panel opens, the FAB unmounts (the panel
553	occupies its anchor); when the panel closes, the FAB re-mounts. Single
554	floating element at any time, no visual stacking.
555	
556	**Header chrome**: **always minimal** — only the `×` close button,
557	right-aligned. No divider, no scope pill. Same treatment for every chat
558	state, identical to the mobile sheet which has no header chrome at all.
559	
560	**Why no scope pill migration**: an earlier draft of this spec moved a
561	scope pill from the entry hero into the header once a conversation
562	began, on the rationale that the popover floats over the host listing
563	page and the user might "lose track" of which listing the bot is
564	grounded on. Two reasons that rationale didn't hold up:
565	
566	1. The host listing-detail page behind the popover is itself the anchor
567	   — title, photos, price, and map are all in the same viewport, visible
568	   alongside the popover at all times. A header scope pill duplicates
569	   information the page is already showing.
570	2. The popover is structurally **listing-page-bound** (`PcAiChat`
571	   instantiates inside `PcListing`, not at the app root), so it cannot
572	   accidentally "follow" the user to a different listing. There is no
573	   architectural path for the popover and the page-behind to disagree
574	   on scope.
575	
576	The entry hero's scope pill (§5.13) still carries the affordance "this
577	chat will be grounded on this listing" before the user commits. Once
578	messages flow, per-bubble Source Label (§5.8) takes over as the
579	finer-grained grounding signal. This makes desktop and mobile
580	symmetric: **scope pill appears only in the entry hero on both surfaces,
581	never in any persistent chrome**.
582	
583	**ESC dismiss**: pressing ESC closes the panel. Mobile sheet has no ESC
584	equivalent (touch-first interaction model).
585	
586	**Mapping to 12-state machine** — same logical states as §4, only the
587	container shell differs:
588	
589	| # | Mobile (Sheet, §5.7) | Desktop (Popover, this section) |
590	|---|---|---|
591	| 1 `trigger` | Host action bar + AI FAB | Fixed bottom-right FAB |
592	| 2 `hint` | Coachmark over FAB | (deferred — desktop FAB visible enough on first load) |
593	| 3 `halfsnap` | Sheet at 50 dvh | **N/A** — popover has no half-snap (opens directly to entry hero) |
594	| 4 `entry_hero` | Sheet full-snap, hero content | Popover at fixed size, hero content + minimal header (`×` only) |
595	| 5 `retrieving` | Sheet full-snap, hero replaced by typing indicator | Popover, hero replaced by typing indicator, header unchanged (`×` only) |
596	| 6 `streaming` | Same body, chrome unchanged | Same body, chrome unchanged |
597	| 7 `stopped` | User tapped stop | Same |
598	| 8 `result` | Assistant bubble landed | Same |
599	| 9 `show_more` | Collapsed bubble expanded | Same |
600	| 10 `abstained` | Abstain marker rendered | Same |
601	| 11 `noresult` | Error bubble inside sheet | Error bubble inside popover |
602	| 12 `error` | Error bubble inside sheet | Error bubble inside popover |
603	
604	**Components reused inside the popover** *(no visual delta from §5.1 - §5.14)*:
605	Message Bubble (§5.1), Suggestion Chip (§5.2), Composer (§5.4), Send/Stop
606	(§5.5), AI Brand Mark (§5.6), Source Label (§5.8), Abstain Marker (§5.9),
607	Typing Indicator (§5.10), Show More Toggle (§5.11), Scope Pill (§5.13),
608	Error Bubble (§5.14). Bubble inner-text wrap, padding, gap, and shape
609	are byte-identical. Only the outer chrome (sheet vs popover) differs.

613	## 6. Component Composition Rules
614	
615	| Inside a chat surface | Outside (host page, search, etc.) |
616	|---|---|
617	| Use this document's tokens | Use `housesigma-design-system.md` |
618	| Soft radii (16-24) | Tight radii (5-13) |
619	| Pill inputs, circular send | Rectangular inputs, square buttons |
620	| Phosphor `star-four` for AI brand | Lucide / custom SVG icons |
621	| `--muted` gray fills | `--card` white fills |
622	| 4 px-grid spacing OK to break for bubble feel | Strict 4 px grid |
623	
624	**Where chat surface ends:**
625	- Sheet / Popover container's edge — anything outside (status bar, app
626	  header, listing content behind the scrim or behind the floating popover)
627	  follows base DS
628	- The AI FAB's container — mobile: host page's action bar; desktop:
629	  free-floating `fixed` slot. The FAB itself follows base DS proportions
630	  in both cases.
631	
632	**Layering rule** (z-index):
633	
634	| Layer | z-index | Surface |
635	|---|---|---|
636	| Page content | base | both |
637	| App header | DS-defined | both |
638	| Coachmark (§5.12) | above app header | mobile |
639	| Scrim (§5.7.2) | above all page content | mobile only — desktop popover has no scrim |
640	| Sheet (§5.7) | above scrim | mobile |
641	| Desktop Popover (§5.16) | 1000 | desktop |
642	| Desktop FAB | 1000 | desktop |
643	| Toast (base DS) | above everything | both |

650	
651	This document specifies **visual + interaction** spec, not data schema.
652	Each implementing chat surface defines its own:
653	- Event names (`onChunk` / `onDone` / `onError` / `onProgress`)
654	- Message field names (`abstained` / `grounding_type` / `follow_ups`)
655	- Error code catalog (specific to its service backend)
656	
657	Components in §5 are schema-agnostic in the following sense:
658	- §5.8 Source Label expects "some enum on done" — it doesn't care if
659	  the field is `grounding_type` or `source_kind`
660	- §5.9 Abstain marker expects "some boolean on done" — `abstained` or
661	  `is_abstain` both work
662	- §5.3 Follow-up chips expect "some string array on done" — `follow_ups`
663	  or `next_questions` both work

occupies its anchor); when the panel closes, the FAB re-mounts. Single
floating element at any time, no visual stacking.

**Header chrome**: **always minimal** — only the `×` close button,
right-aligned. No divider, no scope pill. Same treatment for every chat
state, identical to the mobile sheet which has no header chrome at all.

**Why no scope pill migration**: an earlier draft of this spec moved a
scope pill from the entry hero into the header once a conversation
began, on the rationale that the popover floats over the host listing
page and the user might "lose track" of which listing the bot is
grounded on. Two reasons that rationale didn't hold up:

1. The host listing-detail page behind the popover is itself the anchor
   — title, photos, price, and map are all in the same viewport, visible
   alongside the popover at all times. A header scope pill duplicates
   information the page is already showing.
2. The popover is structurally **listing-page-bound** (`PcAiChat`
   instantiates inside `PcListing`, not at the app root), so it cannot
   accidentally "follow" the user to a different listing. There is no
   architectural path for the popover and the page-behind to disagree
   on scope.

The entry hero's scope pill (§5.13) still carries the affordance "this
chat will be grounded on this listing" before the user commits. Once
messages flow, per-bubble Source Label (§5.8) takes over as the
finer-grained grounding signal. This makes desktop and mobile
symmetric: **scope pill appears only in the entry hero on both surfaces,
never in any persistent chrome**.

**ESC dismiss**: pressing ESC closes the panel. Mobile sheet has no ESC
equivalent (touch-first interaction model).

**Mapping to 12-state machine** — same logical states as §4, only the
container shell differs:

| # | Mobile (Sheet, §5.7) | Desktop (Popover, this section) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 `trigger` | Host action bar + AI FAB | Fixed bottom-right FAB |
| 2 `hint` | Coachmark over FAB | (deferred — desktop FAB visible enough on first load) |
| 3 `halfsnap` | Sheet at 50 dvh | **N/A** — popover has no half-snap (opens directly to entry hero) |
| 4 `entry_hero` | Sheet full-snap, hero content | Popover at fixed size, hero content + minimal header (`×` only) |
| 5 `retrieving` | Sheet full-snap, hero replaced by typing indicator | Popover, hero replaced by typing indicator, header unchanged (`×` only) |
| 6 `streaming` | Same body, chrome unchanged | Same body, chrome unchanged |
| 7 `stopped` | User tapped stop | Same |
| 8 `result` | Assistant bubble landed | Same |
| 9 `show_more` | Collapsed bubble expanded | Same |
| 10 `abstained` | Abstain marker rendered | Same |
| 11 `noresult` | Error bubble inside sheet | Error bubble inside popover |
| 12 `error` | Error bubble inside sheet | Error bubble inside popover |

**Components reused inside the popover** *(no visual delta from §5.1 - §5.14)*:
Message Bubble (§5.1), Suggestion Chip (§5.2), Composer (§5.4), Send/Stop
(§5.5), AI Brand Mark (§5.6), Source Label (§5.8), Abstain Marker (§5.9),
Typing Indicator (§5.10), Show More Toggle (§5.11), Scope Pill (§5.13),
Error Bubble (§5.14). Bubble inner-text wrap, padding, gap, and shape
are byte-identical. Only the outer chrome (sheet vs popover) differs.

---

## 6. Component Composition Rules

| Inside a chat surface | Outside (host page, search, etc.) |
|---|---|
| Use this document's tokens | Use `housesigma-design-system.md` |
| Soft radii (16-24) | Tight radii (5-13) |
| Pill inputs, circular send | Rectangular inputs, square buttons |
| Phosphor `star-four` for AI brand | Lucide / custom SVG icons |
| `--muted` gray fills | `--card` white fills |
| 4 px-grid spacing OK to break for bubble feel | Strict 4 px grid |

**Where chat surface ends:**
- Sheet / Popover container's edge — anything outside (status bar, app
  header, listing content behind the scrim or behind the floating popover)
  follows base DS
- The AI FAB's container — mobile: host page's action bar; desktop:
  free-floating `fixed` slot. The FAB itself follows base DS proportions
  in both cases.

**Layering rule** (z-index):

| Layer | z-index | Surface |
|---|---|---|
| Page content | base | both |
| App header | DS-defined | both |
| Coachmark (§5.12) | above app header | mobile |
| Scrim (§5.7.2) | above all page content | mobile only — desktop popover has no scrim |
| Sheet (§5.7) | above scrim | mobile |
| Desktop Popover (§5.16) | 1000 | desktop |
| Desktop FAB | 1000 | desktop |
| Toast (base DS) | above everything | both |

---

## 7. Implementation Notes

### 7.1 Schema-agnostic design

This document specifies **visual + interaction** spec, not data schema.
Each implementing chat surface defines its own:
- Event names (`onChunk` / `onDone` / `onError` / `onProgress`)
- Message field names (`abstained` / `grounding_type` / `follow_ups`)
- Error code catalog (specific to its service backend)

Components in §5 are schema-agnostic in the following sense:
- §5.8 Source Label expects "some enum on done" — it doesn't care if
  the field is `grounding_type` or `source_kind`
- §5.9 Abstain marker expects "some boolean on done" — `abstained` or
  `is_abstain` both work
- §5.3 Follow-up chips expect "some string array on done" — `follow_ups`
  or `next_questions` both work

content.text:
Root cause: collision is **desktop-only** and **structural** — two independent `position:fixed; right:24; bottom:24` anchors fighting for one corner:
- **Schedule View** pill = host-page commercial CTA (base DS, the booking conversion — highest $ value)
- **AI ✨ FAB** = chat entry (Chat DS §5.16, z-1000)

Neither knows about the other → they stack/overlap. Note: **mobile already avoids this** — §5.15 docks the AI FAB *inside* the host action bar, not free-floating. Only desktop (§5.16) chose a free floater, so only desktop collides.

## Options

| # | Approach | How | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Vertical action stack** (recommended quick fix) | One shared `fixed` container, `flex-direction:column-reverse; gap:12`. Schedule View at bottom (primary, most reachable), AI FAB stacked above. Computed positions → never overlap. | +Both fully visible, predictable, smallest change. −Two floaters add corner weight on short viewports. |
| **B** | **Dock AI into listing toolbar** (most system-coherent) | Add `✨ Ask` to the existing top-right action cluster (Watch ⭐ / Share / ⋮). Desktop mirrors mobile §5.15. Bottom-right becomes Schedule-View-only. | +Zero floating collision, consistent w/ own rule, declutters corner. −Lower discoverability than persistent FAB; trigger (top) far from popover (bottom-right). |
| **C** | **Merge into one control** | C1 segmented pill `[✨ Ask │ 📅 Schedule]`; C2 speed-dial (✨ expands to reveal actions). | −C2 buries the $ CTA behind a tap (hurts conversion). −C1 muddles two intents (support vs convert). Avoid unless co-promoting on purpose. |
| **D** | **Scroll-aware show-one** | AI FAB default; Schedule View slides in near agent/price section, AI collapses to slim tab. | +Never two at once, right intent right moment. −More logic, can feel jumpy, collapsed one loses visibility. |

## Recommendation

**A now, B if you want desktop = mobile parity.** Both kill the root cause (shared layout instead of two blind anchors). Reject C2/D-hiding for anything that demotes Schedule View — it's the conversion CTA.

Concrete for **A**:
```css
.hs-float-stack {            /* one container owns the corner */
  position: fixed; right: 24px; bottom: 24px;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse;  /* CTA at bottom */
  align-items: flex-end; gap: 12px; z-index: 900;
}
/* Schedule View pill = order 1 (bottom, primary) */
/* AI FAB 56×56 = order 2 (above) */
```
Open-panel rule: popover (400×600, z-1000) covers the stack → hide/unmount stack while open; restore on close. Keeps §5.16's "single floating element at any time" true.

## Spec gap

§5.16 "single floating element at any time" only governs **FAB ↔ panel**. It's silent on **host-page CTAs sharing the corner** — that's the hole. Amend: *"AI floating layer reserves a dedicated track; must not share the bottom-right anchor with host CTAs. Define stack order + gap; host floaters hide while panel open."*

Want me to mock A and B in `listing-chatbot-design.pen` (or a quick standalone HTML) so you can compare side-by-side?

### 5.17 Floating Action Stack (Host Corner)

The desktop FAB (§5.16) does **not** own the bottom-right corner alone —
the host listing page anchors its **primary commercial CTA** there too
(e.g. *Schedule View*). Two independent `position: fixed; right: 24px;
bottom: 24px` elements collide blindly: neither measures the other, so
they overlap. This section closes that gap.

**Rule:** the corner is owned by **one** shared stack container — never by
individual `fixed` floaters reaching for the same slot.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Container | `position: fixed; right: 24px; bottom: 24px` |
| Layout | `display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; align-items: flex-end; gap: 12px` |
| Order (bottom → top) | Primary host CTA lowest (closest to cursor) · AI FAB stacked above |
| z-index | 900 (below popover / FAB-open at 1000, so an open panel always covers the stack) |
| Open-panel behavior | Popover (§5.16) covers the corner → hide / unmount the whole stack; restore on close |

**Invariants:**

- No host-page floater may anchor `fixed` to the corner on its own — it
  joins the stack or it does not float. This is the rule the old spec was
  missing: "single floating element at any time" (§5.16) governed only
  FAB ↔ panel, never FAB ↔ host CTA.
- The primary commercial CTA keeps the lowest (most reachable) slot; the
  AI FAB never displaces it. AI is **additive**, not a takeover.
- `column-reverse` makes source order = priority order (CTA first in DOM,
  rendered at the bottom); mounting / unmounting the FAB never shifts the
  CTA's position.
- While the AI panel is open the stack is gone, so stack and panel never
  coexist — the corner holds exactly one AI surface at a time.

**Alternative considered — toolbar dock (Variant B, not adopted):** move
the AI entry into the host action bar (the §5.15 mobile model) and leave
the corner to the CTA alone. Valid when the host wants the corner
single-purpose, but rejected as the default — a persistent FAB
out-discovers a toolbar icon. The stack keeps **both** the FAB's
discoverability and the CTA's primacy.

Schedule 在**底部**，chatbot FAB 在**上面**。更重要的放底部。已经是当前实现（spec §5.17 + pen 都这样）。

为什么底部 = 更重要（违反"列表顶部先读"直觉，但浮动栈是**底部锚定**）：

```
   [ ✦ ]   ← AI FAB（次要，向上堆叠）
   [📅 Schedule View] ← 主 CTA（底部锚点）
   ────────────────── 视口底边 (24px)
```

1. **可达性 (Fitts)** — 右下浮层锚在角上，底部那个最贴角、光标/拇指最近、最省距离。底 = 主。
2. **位置稳定** — 锚点(底)位置固定；上面的项随增删而移动。主 CTA 不该动 → 占底部锚点。次要项浮在上面，移动无所谓。
